핵심이슈.summary:
## 오늘의 한국 경제 흐름 요약

국내 가계부채가 1분기에만 14조 원 증가하며 잔액 2,000조 원에 근접하는 가운데, 증가세 둔화에도 불구하고 부채 총량 자체는 여전히 경계 수준에 머물러 있다. 이에 더해 국토연구원은 한국의 주택 중심 자산 구조가 생산성에 부정적 영향을 미친다고 경고하며, 부동산에 집중된 자원 배분이 경제 체질을 약화시킬 수 있다는 구조적 문제를 제기했다. 통화정책 측면에서는 기대인플레이션 상승을 차단하기 위해 연내 두 차례 금리 인상이 기본 시나리오로 확산되고 있어, 부채 부담과 금리 인상 압력이 동시에 가중되는 상황이다. 한편 5월 주택사업 전망에서는 규제 부담으로 수도권과 지방 간 양극화가 뚜렷해지고 있으며, 대외적으로는 미국 경제가 전례 없는 혼란에 빠졌다는 BofA의 진단과 일본의 외환 개입 본격화 우려까지 겹치며 글로벌 불확실성이 국내 경제에 추가적인 하방 리스크로 작용하고 있다.

key_headlines.title: US 30-Year Treasury Yields Hit 14-Year High Amid Middle East Tensions
key_headlines.summary: US bond yields surged to their highest levels since 2007 as the Iran-US conflict escalates, causing the Nasdaq to decline 0.8% and triggering a broad market selloff on Wall Street.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's household credit expanded by 14 trillion won in Q1, though growth momentum continues to moderate with total credit approaching 2 trillion won. Multiple financial institutions warn of economic turbulence ahead, with Bank of America describing the US economy as facing historic chaos. China's economic recovery shows mixed signals with April unemployment falling to 5.2% but consumption and factory activity slowing. The impact of Samsung Electronics' labor dispute threatens to reduce Korea's growth rate by up to 0.5 percentage points through production disruptions of 30 trillion won.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Japan's Q1 GDP surged 2.1% on an annualized basis with private consumption exceeding expectations, prompting the Bank of Japan to prepare for a June rate hike. South Korea's central bank may accelerate rate increases if Hormuz passage reopens, as the GDP gap between potential and actual growth has already turned positive in Q1. China's government has reaffirmed its commitment to defending economic growth amid signs of slowing momentum. Japan faces stagflation pressures from the US-Iran conflict, with long-term interest rates rising and the government preparing additional monetary tightening.
sections.Financial Markets: US Treasury yields surged dramatically with 30-year bonds reaching 5.197%, their highest level since 2007, driven by inflation concerns from the Middle East conflict and anticipated Federal Reserve rate hikes. The Nasdaq declined 0.8% along with major stock indices as bond yields rose, with the Dow Jones falling 0.65% and S&P 500 dropping 0.67%. The spike in US bond yields has triggered a broader market correction globally as investors reassess risk and interest rate expectations. The financial markets are reacting to the appointment of Kevin Wash as the new Fed chair, raising concerns about political pressure on monetary policy independence.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's semiconductor, shipbuilding, petrochemical, and securities sectors are expected to post record operating profits in Q2. Asset managers are actively competing to identify next-generation AI beneficiary stocks beyond semiconductors, with automotive and physical AI ecosystems gaining focus. European battery manufacturers are facing successive bankruptcies including Sweden's Northvolt and Norway's Morrow, intensifying competition between Korean and Chinese players in EV battery production. Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution are expanding production of battery technologies in Central Europe to secure market position amid changing competitive dynamics.
sections.Real Estate: South Korea's real estate market faces uncertainty in the second half due to reconstruction burden fees and tax reforms. Demographic shifts are occurring with 50-year-olds selling apartments in Seoul while 30-year-olds are increasingly purchasing, ahead of the reinstatement of capital gains tax surcharge on multi-property owners. The diminishing supply of jeonse (key money deposits) contracts is driving younger buyers into the market as traditional deposit-based housing arrangements disappear. Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song is disposing of two of three properties including a Chicago apartment, addressing multi-property ownership controversy.
sections.International Economy: Kevin Wash, the new Federal Reserve chair, assumes office on May 22 at the White House and will preside over his first FOMC meeting on June 16-17. Trump administration officials have criticized the Fed's interest rate policies, with pro-Trump Fed board member Christopher Waller subtly criticizing pressure for rate cuts amid elevated mortgage rates from the Iran conflict. The global financial markets await Wash's monetary policy direction amid political pressure for lower rates and inflation concerns. South Korea's Deputy Prime Minister Gu Yun-chul promoted Korean investment opportunities in London, citing the current period as a golden opportunity for capital market growth.
sections.AI & Economy: Deputy Prime Minister Gu Yun-chul presented Korea's AI hub development initiative to European financial institutions including HSBC and Schroders, aiming to boost investment during what he described as a golden moment for Korean capital markets. Academic experts emphasize the need to reform Korea's labor market for the AI era by increasing flexibility while strengthening social safety nets through extended unemployment benefits. The US model of extended unemployment insurance benefits during recessions is being studied as a potential framework for Korea as AI automation accelerates job market disruption. AI's resource intensity is highlighted, with the technology requiring electricity for computation and water for cooling systems.
sections.Others: Global geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran are impacting economic policy across multiple nations, with concerns that reduced Taiwan arms sales could trigger abandonment of Korea and Japan's security commitments. The 58th Korea-Japan Economic Forum brought 300 executives from both nations to Tokyo to discuss cooperation in AI, robotics, and energy infrastructure. Financial regulators warned against excessive leveraged investment products and potential industry competition distortions ahead of new leverage ETF launches. Jeju International Airport faces operational challenges despite 200 billion won in infrastructure investment, unable to secure additional flight slots for expanded capacity.
